title: Value of the client_secret parameter of an Adobe OAuth Server-to-Server token request
summary: A synthetic value of client_secret beside client_id, grant_type=client_credentials and scope, in a raw form-encoded POST body, a curl -d argument and a query string of the token request.
rationale: The parameter is the carrier: Adobe documents client_secret as a mandatory request parameter of the client_credentials token request, sent in a form-encoded body or as a query parameter, with the body recommended because query parameters may be logged (contract claim s2s-client-secret-request-parameter). Adobe states no prefix, alphabet, length or checksum, so the value is flagged because of the parameter it sits in, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only: the parameter name, the equals sign and the ampersand are outside it, and the client_id beside it is the credential's public identifier (sibling adobe-developer-console-client-id). The p8e- prefix in two rule artifacts is not used: the contract keeps it as an unattributed tool lead (see the not-assertable case for bare prefixed values).

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the client_secret parameter of a client_credentials token request is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Adobe documents client_secret in the form body or query of the token request (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: client_secret is a mandatory parameter described as the value of client secret obtained from the Developer Console; parameters can be sent in the body or as query parameters, and passing parameters in the body is recommended for sensitive data.
sources.locator: section "Fetching access tokens", Parameters table and cURL request

sources.supports: The cURL example posts client_id, client_secret, grant_type=client_credentials and scope as a form-encoded body to the token endpoint, with client_id and client_secret shown as {CLIENT_ID} and {CLIENT_SECRET} placeholders.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
